platform.platform: Linux-5.3.18-59.37-preempt-x86_64-with-glibc2.31
sys.maxsize > 2**32: True
platform.python_version: 3.9.8
cx_Oracle.version: 8.3.0
cx_Oracle.clientversion: (19, 6, 0, 0, 0)

Oracle server 19 EE docker image container-registry.oracle.com/database/enterprise:19.3.0.0



2. Is it an error or a hang or a crash?

Error

3. What error(s) or behavior you are seeing?

Oracle's error code is not set in exception object. This makes harder to get the code value. Especially in sqlachemy cx_oracle dialect. It breaks reconnect workflow.

See [sqlalchemy.dialects.oracle.cx_oracle.OracleDialect_cx_oracle.is_disconnect](https://github.com/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy/blob/ddedc61f9889a35d0f9463fd5f0c46abdfe08285/lib/sqlalchemy/dialects/oracle/cx_oracle.py#L1229) 
```
    def is_disconnect(self, e, connection, cursor):
        (error,) = e.args
        if isinstance(
            e, (self.dbapi.InterfaceError, self.dbapi.DatabaseError)
        ) and "not connected" in str(e):
            return True

        if hasattr(error, "code"):
            # ORA-00028: your session has been killed
            # ORA-03114: not connected to ORACLE
            # ORA-03113: end-of-file on communication channel
            # ORA-03135: connection lost contact
            # ORA-01033: ORACLE initialization or shutdown in progress
            # ORA-02396: exceeded maximum idle time, please connect again
            # TODO: Others ?
            return error.code in (28, 3114, 3113, 3135, 1033, 2396)
        else:
            return False
```

This behavior changed in cx_oracle 8.2.
8.1 is fine.
bug report for sqlachemy https://github.com/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy/issues/7748

try:

body: @zzzeek, ``error.code`` is *only* populated when an Oracle error is generated. It is *not* populated for ODPI-C error messages. If we could go back in time we would populate ``error.code`` with the strings ``ORA-3113``, ``DPI-1010`` or ``DPI-1080``. Changing that now, however, would be disruptive. In our own test suite we are simply examining the beginning of the error message which is always of the form ``XXX-NNNN:`` where ``XXX`` is one of DPI/ORA/etc. and ``NNNN`` is a number. That is likely the best approach to use for you, as well. If you have other suggestions, however, I'd be happy to hear them!

hi Anthony -

well that's what we have to do for now, but I would suggest the possibility of adding other parameters, such as ``error.dpi_code``.     We like to keep away from parsing strings if at all possible as the format of these strings can change.

oh or , of course, if there's a reliable flag like "connection.is_disconnected" or something like that, or more like what we do, on the exception object there's a flag "is_disconnect" which indicates if this error message means the connection has been disconnected or is otherwise no longer usable.

Hmm, no parsing is needed as you just do something like this: ``error.message.startswith("DPI-1080:")``. I agree that it is not as pleasant as ``error.code == 'DPI-1080'`` but we can't use ``error.code`` without disrupting existing code. We could add another attribute, though -- but what to name it?!? Any suggestions? I don't want to have ``error.dpi_code`` as then we would have to add another one for the new thin driver (that is not yet released). The only suggestion I can think of is ``error.full_code`` but I'm not sure how palatable that one is either!

full_code is better, how about a tuple:

``error.full_code = ('DPI', 1080)``

we will go with an equivalent "startswith()" approach for now

**Mike Bayer** has proposed a fix for this issue in the **main** branch:

**support cx_Oracle DPI disconnect codes** https://gerrit.sqlalchemy.org/c/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy/+/3631

**Mike Bayer** has proposed a fix for this issue in the **rel_1_4** branch:

**support cx_Oracle DPI disconnect codes** https://gerrit.sqlalchemy.org/c/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy/+/3632
@zzzeek Thank you for fixing it so quick. Also, I am loving your test code with mock oracle and selective testing on dialects.
